Title: Europe’s Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/europe-industrial-leaders-engineering-manufacturing/

Published Time: 2026-10-21T10:30:40+00:00

Markdown Content:
To increase productivity, accelerate innovation and create new opportunities for economic growth, Europe’s industrial leaders are tapping [NVIDIA CUDA-X](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/technologies/cuda-x/) and [Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse), as well as [NVIDIA Cosmos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/cosmos/) and [Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) open models, across the engineering and manufacturing lifecycle.

Bringing those capabilities together on the factory floor, the [NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX)](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/factory-operations-fox-blueprint-ai-brain/) is now available in [early access on GitHub](http://developer.nvidia.com/factory-operations-blueprint-early-access), providing a path for developers to build and deploy always-on factory manager agents that coordinate work across machines, and specialist agents focused on use cases such as visual inspection, root cause analysis, report generation and fleet management.

These agents can connect to frontier models, including NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron, and foundational knowledge including computer-aided design, product lifecycle management, simulation software, and IT and operational technology systems.

Building on the FOX blueprint enables the ecosystem to build industrial agents that monitor factory operations in real time, correlate visual findings and machine logs to investigate problems, and coordinate responses. With Cosmos in-context learning, these agents can adapt using examples and documentation, without fine-tuning.

[Siemens](https://press.siemens.com/global/en/pressrelease/siemens-partners-nvidia-advance-ai-driven-autonomous-factories) is integrating agents built using FOX into Intelligence Center X, its agentic enterprise system, to help identify root causes and coordinate factory operations, for estimated cost savings of 20%. Siemens’ Process Preparation X agents use [NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-data-factory) tools and skills to generate defect images for circuit-board inspection. At its Erlangen electronics factory, [Siemens](https://news.siemens.com/en-us/siemens-nvidia-pcba-digital-twin-factory/) used this approach to reduce calibration time of inspection processes by 40%.

## **Accelerating Engineering From the First Design**

NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries accelerate simulation, giving engineers faster feedback to explore design alternatives before committing to physical prototypes. At GTC Berlin, [NVIDIA is releasing cuDSS for general availability](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cudss-generally-available-engineering-scientific-simulation), accelerating the demanding calculations behind the complex simulations of structural stress, fluid flow, electromagnetic fields and semiconductor device behavior.

Mercedes-Benz uses Siemens’ Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on NVIDIA GPUs to compare vehicle designs through faster aerodynamic simulations. In factories, the company applies NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and the [Metropolis VSS blueprint](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/video-search-and-summarization) to build agents for vehicle inspection and windshield assembly verification, detecting deviations and ensuring consistently high quality.

[Cadence](https://community.cadence.com/cadence_blogs_8/b/corporate-news/posts/cadence-and-toyota-advance-automotive-simulation-on-nvidia-ai-infrastructure) is benchmarking automotive fluid-dynamics workloads on NVIDIA GPUs to assess opportunities for faster design iteration, while [Autodesk](https://adsknews.autodesk.com/en/news/autodesk-navpack-nvidia/) brings the [NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo](https://developer.nvidia.com/physicsnemo) and [Warp](https://developer.nvidia.com/warp-python) frameworks into NavPack, integrated with Autodesk Alias, to help designers like those at Bentley’s predict vehicle performance and iterate faster using simulation-trained AI.

imec and Infineon are accelerating semiconductor simulation with [Synopsys](https://ansys.synopsys.com/blog/synopsys-advances-physical-ai) software and NVIDIA accelerated computing. Benchmarks of S-Litho on imec’s model show up to 40x speedup, while Infineon uses Sentaurus Device with NVIDIA CUDA libraries to achieve a 12x speedup in 3D breakdown simulation for next-generation power devices.

Leonardo is working with [Neural Concept](https://www.neuralconcept.com/post/leonardo-neural-concept-engineering-ai-aerospace) on AI-driven aircraft design, tapping NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bring aircraft geometry and aerodynamic simulation results together.

Video courtesy of Neural Concept and Leonardo.

Car manufacturers use [Dassault Systèmes](https://blog.3ds.com/topics/company-news/long-running-agents)’ LEO & AURA Virtual Companions, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, and orchestrating CATIA AI Agents & SIMULIA AI Agents with SIMULIA solvers, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, to rapidly design and virtually test vehicle doors before building physical prototypes.

[UniversalAGI](https://www.universalagi.com/research/saab-warfighter) is working with Saab to protect sailors from life-threatending wave impacts at sea, using UniversalAGI’s Latent Interaction Field Transformer physics AI foundation models with accelerated processing by NVIDIA Warp to evaluate thousands of wave conditions and headings in real time instead of days. These capabilities enable vessels to anticipate dangerous motion and autonomously select safer routes to avoid putting sailors at risk, while NVIDIA Omniverse libraries help visualize vessel behavior at sea.

[PhysicsX](http://www.physicsx.ai/newsroom/physicsx-and-gb1-unveil-new-ai-powered-approach-to-americas-cup-yacht-design-at-nvidia-gtc-berlin) is working with GB1, Britain’s America’s Cup team, on AI-powered yacht design, using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to visualize hull geometry and pressure fields, while [Fermioniq](https://fermioniq.com/research-post.html?slug=from-prompt-to-validated-solver-sofia)’s Sofia agent helps Deltares and Dutch ministries model river flow by translating natural-language requests into simulation solvers built on NVIDIA Warp.

Mistral plans to use CUDA-X, Warp and Omniverse libraries to accelerate physics simulation and generate training data for engineering AI models.

## **Testing Factories and Robots Virtually**

NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac libraries enable [digital twins](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/digital-twin/) and [robotics simulation](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/use-cases/robotics-simulation/), helping manufacturers evaluate production systems and robot behavior before making changes on the factory floor.

Video courtesy of Agile Robots, Audi and Dassault Systèmes.

Audi uses a battery-production digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to test production concepts before physical equipment is available. The company is also working with Dassault Systèmes and [Agile Robots](https://www.agile-robots.com/en/news/detail/?tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Bnews_preview%5D=171&cHash=40b4225a49dd14369c63cfce495bbfd5) to simulate and validate mobile humanoid robots and logistics processes in [DELMIA](https://www.agile-robots.com/en/news/detail/?tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Bnews_preview%5D=175&cHash=c7c9b5c85df948b22dbd39e2a4eb91af) virtual twins built with Omniverse libraries.

Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of its humanoid actuators — components that move robot joints — with NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks, helping its robotics partners evaluate component behavior in simulation and reduce physical testing.

At Volkswagen Sachsen’s Transparent Factory, [Wandelbots uses NOVA with Isaac Sim](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/case-studies/volkswagen-with-wandelbots-nova-and-isaac-sim/), built on Omniverse and OpenUSD, to validate assembly workflows digitally and prepare applications for physical robots.

[Falkor](https://falkor.com/news/falkor-demonstrates-spatial-intelligence-for-industrial-ai-agents-with-nvidia-omniverse), a KONGSBERG company, is integrating agents and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries into its platform. With Microsoft Azure NCv6 virtual machines powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, agents with spatial intelligence combine engineering data, operating information and 3D equipment geometry to see, simulate and reason over industrial facilities, supporting inspection and maintenance use cases across the process and energy industries.

Video courtesy of Falkor, a KONGSBERG company.

# NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations

October 21, 2026 by[Timothy Costa](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/timothycosta/ "Posts by Timothy Costa")

 Share

Share This Article

NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an [NVIDIA CUDA-X library](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-x-libraries) that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs.

Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test.

NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost.

Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers:

*   **Applied Materials:**With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability.
*   **COMSOL:** Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours.
*   [**Cadence**](https://community.cadence.com/cadence_blogs_8/b/corporate-news/posts/cadence-and-toyota-advance-automotive-simulation-on-nvidia-ai-infrastructure)**:** Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster.
*   **Dassault Systèmes****:**Dassault Systèmes reports an 8-10x speedup using cuDSS within its Abaqus structural and computer simulation technology electromagnetic solvers for performance-critical simulations across industries.
*   **Siemens****:** Siemens uses cuDSS in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to accelerate simulations of structures in fluid-structure interaction workflows.
*   [**Synopsys**](https://ansys.synopsys.com/blog/synopsys-advances-physical-ai)**:**Synopsys uses cuDSS in its Sentaurus Device simulator tool to accelerate simulations of advanced logic, memory and power chips, helping Infineon model increasingly complex devices faster.

## **Accelerated Simulation at Scale**

As simulation workloads grow in size and complexity, cuDSS can scale out of the box from individual workstations to large computing clusters.

Developers can integrate cuDSS into existing engineering, scientific and optimization software offerings, bringing GPU acceleration to tools already used by engineers and researchers. They can use cuDSS through C, C++, Python and Fortran interfaces.

# NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure

 New Confidential Bare Metal with NVIDIA Confidential Computing protects models and data across cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure — plus, NVIDIA Confidential Computing is expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems as well as NVIDIA DSX OS.

October 21, 2026 by[John Fanelli](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/johnfanelli/ "Posts by John Fanelli")

 Share

Share This Article

NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents [across the stack](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ai-security-agent-stack/). The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, [announced today](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/openshell-reference-architecture), is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. [NVIDIA Confidential Computing](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/solutions/confidential-computing/) is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running.

Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data.

NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure.

NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options:

*   Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure
*   Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments
*   Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments

Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements.

NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories.

## **Model Builders Tap Global Capacity**

Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide.

Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution.

“Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.”

Google Cloud is extending support for Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property.

“Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud.

## **Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform**

NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution.

Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems.

[CoreWeave](https://www.coreweave.com/blog/coreweave-zero-trust-ai-framework-your-model-your-data-your-trust), Firmus, GMI Cloud, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Microsoft Azure Infrastructure,Nebius, Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. # NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Expands, Grounding Enterprise Agents in Company Data

October 21, 2026 by[Erik Pounds](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/epounds/ "Posts by Erik Pounds")

 Share

Share This Article

Agents are only as useful as what they know, and only as trustworthy as the boundaries they run within.

Leading enterprises are using the open source NVIDIA Agent Toolkit — now expanded with new tools — to customize and control agents, use company data to inform their answers and actions, monitor what they do and govern how they operate.

NVIDIA Agent Toolkit comprises:

*   The new [NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation](https://developer.nvidia.com/topics/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation) with NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries
*   NVIDIA open models including Nemotron Retriever and the new [Kumo](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/open-models-europe-industry) family
*   [NVIDIA OpenShell](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/openshell-reference-architecture) secure agent runtime
*   [NVIDIA NemoClaw](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/nemoclaw/) secure agent blueprints
*   Tools and skills, like NeMo Relay and NeMo Compass

To develop agents that accomplish real work and are trustworthy from development to deployment, builders need an open agent stack that brings together the models, harness, runtime, data and tools.

NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation helps enterprises turn data into company intelligence agents can use. Agents can find relevant information, understand what it means for the business and use it to make predictions and help people decide what to do next. Companies can use Agent Knowledge Foundation without moving data, rebuilding existing workflows or changing governance controls.

The foundation features [NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/technologies/cuda-x/), including cuDF, cuGraph, cuML, cuOpt and cuVS, and the new [Auto-Ontology](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology) library, which translates raw company data into familiar business concepts — like customers, products and orders — and maps how they relate.

It also includes [NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever](https://developer.nvidia.com/topics/ai/nemotron) and [Kumo Structured](https://developer.nvidia.com/topic/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation/kumo/) open models — Kumo Tabular, Kumo Relational, Kumo Time Series and Kumo Forecast — which help agents find relevant company information to answer questions and make predictions.

OpenShell provides the secure runtime boundary, giving enterprises control over what agents can access and do. NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints provide reference designs for building secure, specialized agents. The newest [NemoClaw](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemoclaw-for-agent-optimization) blueprint for agent optimization provides a step-by-step starting point for improving agent intelligence — making them better at their jobs over time.

## **Enterprises Adopt NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation**

The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation is already at work across enterprises.

With Palantir, [NVIDIA’s supply chain organization](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-palantir-bring-sovereign-intelligence-to-critical-supply-chains) is using Agent Knowledge Foundation through Palantir Foundry, Ontology and AIP to deploy specialized agents, create actionable intelligence from proprietary data, predict outcomes and optimize decision-making.

[Databricks](http://databricks.com/blog/databricks-ai-runtime-nvidia-train-fine-tune-models)pairs NVIDIA Kumo Anomaly with Databricks Genie Ontology to power context-aware agents.

[Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/nvidia-kumo-graph-ml-snowflake/) is enabling customers to use the NVIDIA Kumo Engine and Kumo Relational open models in their Snowflake Notebook environments to unlock more predictive capabilities.

NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models make search faster and more accurate. Using the embedding model, [Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://opensearch.org/blog/nvidia-nemotron-embeddings-for-agentic-search-in-opensearch/) improved relevance with fewer search steps and virtually no added latency. [SAP](https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-sap/sap-and-nvidia-training-compact-instruction-following-rerankers-using-opd/ba-p/14506708)’s fine-tuned reranker ran nearly 3x faster. ServiceNow improved reranking quality while cutting latency by nearly a quarter. Zoom is using Nemotron Retriever models to improve document understanding, search relevance and context retrieval for Zoom AI Services.

Amazon Web Services (AWS), ClickHouse, Cloudera, [Cohesity](https://www.cohesity.com/blogs/bring-relevant-enterprise-context-to-ai-agents-with-cohesity-and-nvidia/), [Dassault Systèmes](https://blog.3ds.com/topics/company-news/long-running-agents), Dell,[Elastic](https://www.elastic.co/blog/elastic-nvidia-cuvs-integration), Exa, IBM, NetApp, Oracle, Perplexity, [Starburst](http://starburst.io/press-release/starburst-introduces-torin-gpu-native-analytics-engine-built-on-nvidia-cudf) and [VAST Data](http://www.vastdata.com/blog/building-semantic-enterprise-search-for-ai-agents)are also among those building on Agent Knowledge Foundation.

_Learn more by joining this_[_GTC Berlin session on building, deploying and optimizing specialized agents in production_](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/gtc/session-catalog/sessions/gtceu26-sb61091/)_._

Title: NVIDIA Open Models Advance Europe’s Sovereign Intelligence Across Industries

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/open-models-europe-industry/

Published Time: 2026-10-21T10:00:07+00:00

Markdown Content:
NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing, giving developers, researchers and enterprises what they need to build applications tailored to local languages and industries

The portfolio includes the new [NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nemotron-3-5-super-vl/) models; new [NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/nemotron-retriever-world-class-agentic-retrieval) models for embedding, reranking and document parsing; the new [NVIDIA Kumo](https://developer.nvidia.com/topic/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation/kumo/) family open weight foundation models and libraries for structured business data; [NVIDIA Cosmos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/cosmos/) 3.5 world models; [NVIDIA Alpamayo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/alpamayo/) 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles; [NVIDIA BioNeMo](https://github.com/NVIDIA-BioNeMo) for healthcare and scientific discovery; and [NVIDIA Ising](https://developer.nvidia.com/ising) for quantum computing.

The open models give organizations a foundation they can customize with local data and deploy on infrastructure they control.

## **NVIDIA Nemotron Powers Post-Training Across Industries**

NVIDIA Nemotron brings open language models, datasets and recipes to developers building agents. The models support text and images, helping agents orchestrate workflows, reason through complex problems and complete specialized tasks at a lower cost. Nemotron models are built with data, research and expertise from the [NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-launches-nemotron-coalition-of-leading-global-ai-labs-to-advance-open-frontier-models), including European partners Black Forest Labs, H-Company and Mistral.

Nemotron provides a foundation for enterprises to build applications based on their own knowledge and expertise. [Dassault Systèmes](https://blog.3ds.com/topics/company-news/long-running-agents), Domyn, Dream, Palantir’s customers, Salesforce, SAP, Shopify, Synopsys and [WPP](https://research.wpp.com/blog/crossing-the-real-time-agentic-threshold-benchmarking-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-on-google-cloud-a5x-powered-by-nvidia-vera-rubin-nvl72), as well as professional services providers like Accenture and EY, are working with Nemotron models and datasets to create custom models and build domain-specific agents.

A broad ecosystem of post-training partners, including AfterQuery, AgileRL, AI21, Alice, Applied Compute, Baseten, CoreWeave,Distil Labs, EON, Fastino, Fireworks,Google Cloud, Mercor, Multiverse Computing, Nebius, Handshake AI, Plurai,Prime Intellect, River.AI,Scale AI, Trajectory and TNG, is helping enterprises customize Nemotron for domain-specific workloads.

## **NVIDIA Kumo Speeds Agents’ Work With Structured Enterprise Data**

[NVIDIA Kumo](https://developer.nvidia.com/topic/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation/kumo/) open foundation models, libraries and tools help agents and applications forecast outcomes, score fraud risk and recommend actions from structured business data. Part of [NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation](https://developer.nvidia.com/topics/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation), Kumo shortens time to prediction and reduces the cost and complexity of building a separate machine learning pipeline for every task.

Developers can use pretrained Kumo models to bring predictions to more applications quickly, then fine-tune them using proprietary data when higher performance is critical. The portfolio includes [NVIDIA Kumo Structured](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nvidia-kumo-structured), with models for relational and tabular prediction, forecasting and anomaly detection, and [NVIDIA Kumo Engine](https://github.com/NVIDIA/kumo-engine), an open library stack for developing and deploying structured data foundation models.

[Cognite](https://www.cognite.com/en/partners/nvidia), Coinbase, Databricks, DoorDash, Revolut and Tubi are among the first to work with Kumo models to accelerate development. Snowflake customers are already using Kumo models to accelerate AI development in industries including advertising, energy, financial services and retail.

## **NVIDIA Cosmos Accelerates Robotics Training and Simulation**

NVIDIA Cosmos is a family of open world foundation models that helps developers build robots, autonomous vehicles and vision agents that understand and interact with the physical world.

NVIDIA is introducing new Cosmos post-training and optimization tools to help developers improve world models using less compute, along with simulation checkpoints for evaluating behavior in interactive driving and robotic manipulation scenarios before real-world testing.

NVIDIA is also introducing Cosmos Data Factory — comprising blueprints and core agent skills — to help developers curate, label, generate and evaluate training data for driving scenarios, product defects, image augmentation and event generation. Developers can use complete workflows or individual capabilities with agents coordinating the process.

Porsche with Voxel51, [ANYbotics with Encord](https://encord.com/data-labs/nvidia-anybotics-synthetic-data/), Zalando and CEVA Logistics with Sereact, and [Siemens](https://news.siemens.com/en-us/siemens-nvidia-pcba-digital-twin-factory/) are using Cosmos Data Factory to create high-quality, diverse training datasets and improve model precision.

## **NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Brings Real-Time Reasoning to Autonomous Vehicles**

NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is a compact reasoning model that brings real-time scene understanding and motion planning directly into autonomous vehicles. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos and optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor platform, it helps developers bring advanced driving capabilities into vehicles with lower computing requirements.

## **NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina Advances Protein Design**

NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina is an open protein design model from NVIDIA and the Baker Lab at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design.

The model generates protein sequences and 3D structures to help researchers design proteins that bind to difficult targets, assemble into complex structures and bind to small molecules.

NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina delivers leading performance across more than 10 protein design tasks and generates designs about 13x faster than RFdiffusion3 in a benchmark of 200 amino acid proteins. Researchers can use the model through agents to generate and evaluate candidates against design goals and molecular constraints, then choose which designs to test in the lab.

## **NVIDIA Ising Accelerates Quantum Development**

The NVIDIA Ising family of open models provides a common, extensible foundation to speed the breakthroughs needed to develop useful quantum supercomputers, from real-time hardware calibration to error correction, across different qubit modalities and tailored to individual hardware needs.

IQM Quantum Computers is using Ising to calibrate its quantum processors, showcasing how specialized open calibration models outperform large general-purpose models. SEEQC is combining the NVIDIA NVQLink platform and Ising with its unique Digital Link to meet the low-latency requirements needed for real-time quantum error correction.

[AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/quantum-computing/decoding-quantum-errors-with-nvidia-ising-decoding-on-aws/) is making NVIDIA Ising readily available to researchers by integrating the model family into AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS). While decoding is typically performed on classical hardware colocated with the quantum processor due to latency requirements, the AWS PCS integration lets researchers build on Ising prior to deployment.

## **Availability**

*   **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL**is available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4), [ModelScope](https://modelscope.ai/collections/nv-community/Nemotron-35-Lightning), [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free) and [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b) as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as through NVIDIA cloud, post-training and inference partners. **Nemotron 3.5 Bolt** E4B 4GB is expected to be available on Friday, Oct. 23.
*   **NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever** open models are available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-retriever), various partner platforms, and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice on [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/explore/retrieval).
*   **NVIDIA Kumo** open models are available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nvidia-kumo-structured) and optimized and packaged as an NVIDIA NIM microservice for production inference on [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/explore/predictive-ai).
*   **NVIDIA Cosmos** is now openly available on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3) and [GitHub](https://github.com/nvidia/Cosmos), and through select inference partners.
*   **NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge** will be available for download on GitHub and Hugging Face later this month.
*   The **NVIDIA BioNeMo**open model RFD4-Proteina is available on [build.nvidia.com](http://build.nvidia.com/) and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as on GitHub, Hugging Face and through select inference partners.
*   **NVIDIA Ising**is available on GitHub, Hugging Face and [build.nvidia.com](http://build.nvidia.com/).

Markdown Content:
Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events.

Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle.

GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote.

## **Huang Takes the Stage**

Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said.

The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly [$10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/france-ecosystem-agentic-computing/) and working with 12,000+ partners.“After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said.

[AI is a five-layer cake](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ai-5-layer-cake/), Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application.

“Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid.

“To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.”

## **The AI Factory Gets a New Form Factor**

Huang framed NVIDIA’s full-stack AI factory — spanning hardware, system software, CUDA-X libraries and models — as a broad platform for building and operating AI infrastructure.

“This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.”

He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings.

Next, Huang announced [NVIDIA DSX POD](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-introduces-dsx-pod-ai-factories-to-accelerate-europes-infrastructure-deployment), a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. With DSX POD, onsite deployment can shrink from six months to just 14 days once site utilities are ready.

“This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain,” Huang said. “This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up.”

The [NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-ecosystem-builds-worlds-most-efficient-ai-factories-with-nvidia-dsx) enables companies to reduce water consumption for cooling by up to 100% and generate the same AI output with up to 30% less power.

## **Agents Are the New Computing Platform — and Safety Is an Engineering Problem**

Huang said agents think, reason, iterate and use tools, driving token consumption as they become more useful.

He described an agent as comprising five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates its work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge and tools. In that framing, an agent is more than a model answering questions; it can draw on knowledge and act through tools.

“The most important thing is to make sure the agent is secure,” Huang said. The autonomous agent can access files, resources, networks and tools, so its privileges should be minimal and it should be monitored.

NVIDIA’s answer is the new [NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/openshell-reference-architecture), a full-stack design built on [NVIDIA OpenShell](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/openshell/) — an open source, policy-controlled runtime with kernel-level sandboxing that sits between an agent and the systems it can affect.

That means privileges, policy enforcement and monitoring must adapt dynamically. “Every single time an agent is launched, the privileges are different,” Huang said.

## **Open Models Turn Expertise Into an Advantage**

Huang [presented NVIDIA’s open models](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/open-models-europe-industry/) as a starting point for building AI tailored to specific needs.

NVIDIA’s frontier, open models are available for use across industries: Nemotron for language, Cosmos for world foundation models, GR00T for humanoid robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles, Ising for quantum-classical computing and Earth-2 for physics AI.

“We are the frontier,” Huang said. “So in all of these different areas, we offer you all of the models, and we’re continuously working on it. We’ve been working on it for a decade, and we’ll continue to work on this forever.”

NVIDIA provides the models, data and scripts to reproduce them, and companies can post-train a model on their own data for a particular use case — turning proprietary data into what he called “sovereign intelligence.”

“You could start with an open model, something that’s incredibly good like Nemotron, and with your own data, post-train it for your use case and achieve, of course, super intelligence,” Huang said. “That is a very sensible thing to do, and all the technology exists today.”

## **NVIDIA Gives Agents a Knowledge Layer**

Huang then introduced the [NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation](https://developer.nvidia.com/topics/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation) as a set of models and libraries for connecting agents to enterprise data, whether it’s unstructured information in documents or structured data in databases.

He highlighted Nemotron tools for parsing documents, embedding queries and reranking relevant information, along with new [NVIDIA Kumo](https://developer.nvidia.com/topics/ai/agent-knowledge-foundation/kumo) models for making predictions from structured data.

“Ultimately, what turns these super agents, these agents into super agents, is that you give them access to your company’s knowledge,” Huang said.

## **NVIDIA CUDA-X — Accelerated Tools for Agents**

Huang then described [NVIDIA CUDA-X](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/technologies/cuda-x/) as a collection of accelerated libraries used across science, engineering, research and creative work.

NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform has more than 11 million developers building on it.

Huang said those libraries can accelerate simulators, solvers and data-processing engines — the kinds of tools agents may draw on to do useful work.

“CUDA-X tools are what gives agents the tools of the trade,” Huang said.

## **Agents Go to Work in Labs, Factories and Engineering**

A video showcased [NVIDIA Agent Toolkit](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/enterprise-platforms-agent-toolkit/) bringing company knowledge, models and tools together in three industry examples:

At Lila Sciences, agents help design a potential B-cell lymphoma therapy, using virtual experiments to guide work in an automated lab.

At Siemens’ Erlangen factory, agents help prepare new products for production, testing plans in a digital twin before changes reach the factory floor.

And at Dassault Systèmes, engineering agents adapt vehicle design, using simulation to identify a problem and refine the design.

“And [all this] knowledge and tools belong to you,” Huang said after the video rolled. “That’s your expertise, and so all of this is now possible to do.”

## **Telcos as Distributed AI Infrastructure**

Huang said AI is transforming telecommunications, improving spectrum efficiency and turning cell towers into distributed AI infrastructure.

He cited 100,000 sites and about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers, and said [NVIDIA has made its first commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-nokia-and-leading-telecom-operators-turn-networks-into-distributed-intelligence-platforms) after nearly eight years of work.

“Now CUDA makes phone calls,” Huang said. “AI will revolutionize the way we do telecommunications. It will enhance our spectrum efficiency tremendously.”

## **AI Moves Into the Treatment Room**

[Healthcare and life sciences leaders are building on NVIDIA technologies](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/healthcare-and-life-sciences-leaders-build-on-nvidia-to-advance-drug-discovery-and-expand-patient-care) to advance drug discovery and expand patient care.

For example, NVIDIA and Siemens Healthineers are developing AI-enabled radiation therapy.

Nemotron agents coordinate treatment planning, the Isaac for Healthcare platform and Omniverse libraries create a digital twin of the device and patient anatomy to simulate tumor targeting. Holoscan with IGX Thor connects live imaging and sensor data to enable real-time adaptive delivery as the patient moves.

Huang described adaptive radiotherapy as a physical-AI application: as the patient’s body and tumor change during treatment, the system must track the changes and adjust the radiation targeting.

“The tumor is changing in shape. The physical body is changing while you’re in therapy,” Huang said. “The robot, this radio adaptive radiotherapy system, has to perceive the changing environment, understand where the tumor is, segment it just perfectly and direct the radiotherapy accordingly.”

## **The Road Ahead: Mobility Leaders Join NVIDIA’s Automotive Ecosystem******

Huang said the [NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform is being designed into more vehicle fleets](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-mobility-leaders-build-safe-vehicles-and-robotaxi-fleets-on-nvidia-hyperion), with autonomous-driving software connecting robotaxis to ride-hailing services.

Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets.

In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles at scale.

Volkswagen’s van, JLR, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz’s next-generation vehicles will be Hyperion-compatible, Huang announced, saying, “Welcome to Hyperion.”

## **A Reference Humanoid for Robotics Researchers**

Huang then [announced Agile ONE SN](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-advances-isaac-platform-for-general-purpose-robotics-with-new-reference-humanoid-frameworks-simulation-pipelines-and-data), a reference humanoid built on Isaac GR00T — a 31-degree-of-freedom body, expected to be available next year, designed to cut researcher setup time from weeks to days.

The platform is modular: researchers can use the full workflow or pull in selected components.
“This is a great starting point,” Huang said.

articles.content:
Private equity giant Blackstone is putting itself at the center of the AI boom, firm veteran Jas Khaira discussed last week on stage
at TechCrunch Disrupt.
It is writing checks via various strategies, ranging from offering massive loans to data centers to investing in frontier AI models and applications.
Earlier this year, the firm launched Blackstone N1 (BXN1), a San Francisco-based central hub for its AI initiatives. The group is led by Khaira, who relocated from New York to be at the epicenter of AI.
Unlike earlier tech cycles such as mobile or SaaS, which allowed companies to reach significant scale with moderate capital, the transition to AI requires staggering amounts of investment. That need for capital is precisely why Blackstone, with its $1.3 trillion in assets under management, could play such a critical role in this tech shift.
Khaira emphasized that Blackstone sets itself apart from traditional venture capitalists through its focus on compute financing and its ability to offer flexible capital structures, ranging from debt to equity. And it has been investing aggressively.
“We’re the largest owner of compute outside of the hyperscalers today, whether it’s investments in neo clouds, investments in data centers, and being able to use that compute strategically to support companies,” Khaira said.
For instance, BXN1 played a key role in several compute-related deals, among them
Crux AI,
a neocloud launched in partnership with Google to commercialize its custom TPUs, to which Blackstone committed $5 billion as an investor. It also backed
four-year-old Etched
, a chip startup whose rapid development has caught investor attention. Neoclouds are cloud providers that rent out AI GPU infrastructure.
Blackstone pioneered a financing structure that allowed it to lend massive sums to venture-backed cloud neoclouds by analyzing both committed customer contracts and using GPUs pledged as collateral.
Blackstone’s first such deal came in 2023 with CoreWeave, shortly after that neocloud saw demand explode following the launch of ChatGPT. Despite having only “30 million of revenue and minimal profitability” at that time, according to Khaira, CoreWeave approached Blackstone for a $2.3 billion loan.
CoreWeave was borrowing against the considerable value of its large collection of Nvidia GPUs, with Nvidia also an investor. Blackstone also grew more comfortable with the loan because CoreWeave had contracts
with blue-chip customers like Microsoft.
That transaction quickly became the financing model for how Blackstone and other credit institutions provided billions in follow-on debt to CoreWeave and rival neoclouds.
“One of the primary things that we’re looking to is the nature of the customer. And if the customer is an investment-grade customer — let’s say it’s Microsoft or let’s say it’s Meta — the risk gets priced relative to that customer,” Khaira said.
Building on its success with CoreWeave, Blackstone struck other neocloud financing deals, including co-leading alongside Coatue a
$10 billion credit facility
for Australian GPU provider Firmus earlier this year.
Khaira acknowledged that in recent weeks, the large debt burdens accumulated by these companies and other neocloud operators have begun to raise red flags. Coreweave’s debt alone has since
ballooned to about $50 billion
, causing Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner to note in a recent CNBC interview, “The collateral that CoreWeave is putting up which is really only GPUs is not good enough anymore. They used that in the past to get cheap debt.”
Khaira said that on the credit side, the market jitters stem from a combination of factors. Interest rates ticked up in September, and hotter-than-expected inflation signals that borrowing costs may keep climbing. The flood of AI infrastructure debt offerings isn’t helping either.
“We’re also seeing higher credit spreads,” Khaira said, explaining that lenders are charging higher premiums on top of already higher base interest rates to finance the AI buildout. “The cost of capital to price in debt for a Meta or a Microsoft has widened out,” he added, pointing out that even tech giants with massive balance sheets and solid earnings are paying more to borrow.
Concerns about the rising cost of debt have spilled into the stock market. Shares of CoreWeave dropped over 20% in recent days, while
Firmus scrapped
its planned IPO on the Australian Securities Exchange at a target valuation of roughly $30 billion.
“Ultimately, the market wasn’t there at that valuation, and so I think as a result, that deal didn’t get done,” Khaira said about Firmus’ cancelled listing.
“The market is thinking what is the right price for neoclouds, what is the right price for these businesses in this moment when interest rates are moving up,” he said.
Despite those pressures on some infrastructure providers, AI companies simply can’t get enough compute to power their models. Their appetite continues to drive data center buildout.
Khaira downplayed worries of doom-mongers that the massive accumulation of AI infrastructure debt could lead to a widespread credit crisis, or worse, crash the economy altogether. “This doesn’t feel like something where you’ve got 2008 banks that are shaky credits,” he said.
Instead, he pointed out that because the vast majority of data centers are built for hyperscalers, the debt financing them is ultimately backed “by the most creditworthy companies in the world.”
Beyond funding data centers, Blackstone is helping companies adopt AI through a
$1.5 billion joint venture
called “Ode with Anthropic,” formed alongside Anthropic and Hellman & Friedman this year. Ode supplies forward-deployed engineers to help companies adopt AI and integrate it into their operations, starting with Blackstone’s 280 portfolio companies.
When asked if Blackstone-owned companies are seeing tangible gains from AI, Khaira conceded that “there is definitely ROI, but it is uneven.” He described technology adoption as something that could move in a “sawtooth-type pattern,” which, to skeptics, can look like an oversupply of compute before adoption catches up.

articles.content:
TechCrunch Founder Summit
is a full-day gathering in Boston on November 4 where founders across all stages connect with top VCs and experienced entrepreneurs to gain tactical insights on building and scaling their companies. It’s the latest in our long line of founder-centric events, which are smaller and more hands-on than Disrupt.
For the founder looking to really get in the weeds during a one-day crash course, Founder Summit is the ideal place to get a head start on your 2027 plans for everything from hiring, establishing product market fit, finding investors, improving your leadership skills, and more.
Before you dig in on the event details, you can get info on all of our tickets, which are available for a $100 discount for investors and founders,
right here
. Even if you’re a student and an aspiring founder, or an investor looking to meet the next wave of East Coast innovators, we have an option for you.
Who is TechCrunch Founder Summit for?
All founders end up wrestling with the extensive, complicated mechanics of building a company from the ground up. There’s fundraising, hiring, legal, marketing, PR, and leadership, as well as the investors needing the means to vet, invest in, and develop founders as they build out their skills.
Founder Summit is the best way to cover all of the challenging questions with community members who have been there, and lived to tell the tale, through constructive failure and massive success.
When and where is TechCrunch Founder Summit?
The event takes place on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at the
SoWa Power Station
in Boston. It’s accessible via public transportation and a short walk from the Back Bay and Tufts Medical Center stops on the Orange Line, or the Broadway stop on the Red Line.
Image Credits:
TechCrunch / Getty Images
What’s on the TechCrunch Founder Summit agenda?
To deliver on that promise of equipping founders for success,
this year’s agenda
and
speakers
lean hard into fundraising, AI-native building, and leadership. Sessions include:
Building a Company That Keeps Reinventing Itself:
Toast
Co-founder and Director
Steve Fredette
shares his insights on keeping a company relevant amid evolving technologies and changing customer expectations.
The Boston Founder Playbook
:
HqO
co-founder and CEO
Chase Garbarino
on building a category-defining company outside Silicon Valley, having raised $200 million and scaled to 30+ countries.
Finding Product Market Fit Before You Scale
:
Bessemer Venture Partners
‘
Kent Bennett
on validating demand and avoiding scaling before the fundamentals are in place.
Built for AI From Day One
:
7AI
co-founder and CEO
Lior Div
on what changes when AI is the foundation of a company rather than a bolt-on feature.
Not Every Dollar Is Equal
:
Cogent Security
co-founder and CEO
Vineet Edupuganti
on evaluating investors and cap-table trade-offs beyond valuation.
How to Spot the ‘King of the Hill’ Company
:
TDK Ventures
investment director
Tina Tosukhowong
unpacking a framework for evaluating startups on economics, scalability, and timing.
Your Pitch Has to Near the Next Conversation
:
TrueVentures
Partner and
Edisyl
CEO
Dave Balter
instills the importance of making sure your pitch doesn’t just wow, but that it sparks a continued conversation throughout every minute of its delivery.
Is there a pitch competition?
We’re glad you asked! Founder Summit will once again feature the much-requested So You Think You Can Pitch? competition, during which three early stage startups will try to impress a panel of judges within four minutes each. Their approaches, and the judges’ feedback, is invaluable for improving your own pitches.
Didn’t this event have a different name?
Yes. Founder Summit was formerly known as
Early Stage
and
All Stage
. This year, we have the same mission, but with a new name. Keep that in mind if you want to do any more research before attending.
Is TechCrunch Founder Summit just panels, or is there more to it?
Founder Summit is far from a series of panels, though the agenda does provide a ton of valuable insights for founders and investors. In addition to all of those sessions, we also have our breakout sessions, where even more intimate panels discuss vital topics for the community to dive deeper into.
There’s also networking available via the Braindate app to help connect investors with founders, or facilitate founders with similar challenges to bring their expertise together to reach shared solutions. Or that time is the perfect opportunity for students to build out their nascent network.
Then there’s Founder Summit week, taking place November 1-7. That’s when
all of our Side Events are held
, expanding the opportunities for you to gather with the community. And if you’re especially eager to take part, you can apply to host your own Side Event
right here
.
Image Credits:
Halo Creative
How much does a ticket cost, and how can I get the best price?
Pricing moves in phases, with our next increase happening after October 16.
Our current pricing tiers are Investor for $399, Founder for $199, and students for $149
. If you buy a second ticket for a co-founder or co-worker, you’ll also get 50% off their admission. And bundles for groups for four or more offer additional discounts.
Is there a free way to attend?
Yes! We’re looking for volunteers to help staff the event, and those individuals will get a behind-the-scenes look at how the event comes together on top of their free access to programming beyond their shift. Learn more about our program, which closes to new applicants October 19,
right here
.
Where can I register and learn more?
You can get the full rundown of the event, with everything from up-to-date speaker information, the full agenda, logistics, and more
right here
. Ticket information across all three tiers is
available here
. And remember, our current discounts end October 16 — act now before they expire.

Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming
estimates released earlier this week
by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
But it is how people are using it, and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention.
He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent, had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders.
“Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping.
Beyond shopping, Zuckerberg said other popular uses for Muse include personal productivity tasks, such as connecting the AI agent to users’ email or calendars. The exec stressed that this indicates users trusted Muse’s security setup, which includes a feature called “Muse Secure VM” designed to protect their data and privacy. He also mentioned that the forthcoming “Muse Confidential VM” will prevent even Meta from seeing users’ content.
Now that Muse has achieved “product-market fit,” Zuckerberg said Meta’s focus will shift to scaling the AI agent, increasing revenue, and optimizing its compute costs. Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said.
Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users, but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform. Power users who want access to the most advanced AI models or more tokens will also have to pay.
Zuckerberg also noted that Meta believes Muse will be profitable after it scales.
“On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years,” he told bankers and analysts on the Q3 earnings call. “In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.”
Muse will also play a central role in Meta’s smart glasses strategy. Reality Labs, the division responsible for smart glasses, VR, and the metaverse, is still losing billions. However, the
division’s losses
are expected to improve from $19.1 billion in 2025 to $15 billion this year.
Beyond scaling and supporting its hardware strategy, Zuckerberg teased the company’s plans for something he called the “Muse network.” He described this as taking Muse from a “single-player game” to one where “your Muses can work with your friends’ and your families’ [Muses].”
“And if you want to buy something, it’s not just navigating to that business’s website; it’s talking to their agent,” he added.

articles.content:
Recursive
, an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model,
Flint
, on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI.
Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months.
Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop.
The company emerged from stealth in May with
$650 million in funding
at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist.
Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the
usage fees
that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open-source license that allows free use and modification.
Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s
Muse Spark Open
, an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory.
Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second.
On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint.
The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants, and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive.  Wired’s Will Knight
used
Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time.
The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s
launch video
, it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pre-training to post-training and inference.
Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations.
Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said
last month
that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays for every one worked by a human researcher.
If Recursive’s bet pays off, each new model should be able to take on longer stretches of work without human help. The company previously
told TechCrunch
that its $410 million compute deal with Amazon Web Services in June was “less about headcount and more about agent count.”
The longer-term goal, Socher told Wired, is for the Eureka Machine to achieve full recursive self-improvement, with humans overseeing the process and able to stop it if something goes wrong. Recursive says each new model should make the Eureka Machine a better researcher, helping it build the next one faster.

articles.content:
Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor,
Amazon, began blocking AI agents
from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.
The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by
locking them out of their websites completely
. Walmart, on the other hand, had already
announced
a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.
Now it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart president and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club.
It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.
What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent.
The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do.
With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.
The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified and you can cap their spending.
The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary.
Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent.
Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site.

articles.content:
The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out
an alarming warning
on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already
issued by the PHP Foundation
.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers
roughly 70% of the websites
on the internet; by some accounts, that’s
more than 33 million sites
. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.
The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.
Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.
So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz.
Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed
in a blog post
. Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP.
Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws. Then they all worked together to flesh out what they found, and test the patches, drawing in a host of others to help.
Wiz thanked Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare, Fastly, Imperva, Microsoft, and Vercel. (While WordPress sites use PHP, WordPress
has issued a statement
saying that the flaw isn’t WordPress specific, and sites running its CMS must patch their servers and work with their web-hosting companies to ensure their sites are protected.)
OpenAI says that these flaws were found by researchers before hackers discovered them. So there were no reports of exploits in the wild. This is also in part because, before AI, these flaws were too hard for hackers to exploit. “With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts,”
Wiz warned in its blog
about the flaws.
In other words, this is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented because of AI, but is also a high risk only because of AI.
Now that the issue has been disclosed, hackers are fully in the know. The race is on for the internet to patch tens millions of websites before hackers can attack the unpatched ones. Hence the NSA’s guidance that if you can’t patch your PHP website right away, you’re better off pulling it offline until you can.

articles.content:
Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers.
More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and senior managers across seven countries,
commissioned
by work-management company Monday.com. The reason is that much of employees’ output now arrives polished in the manager’s inbox, making it hard to tell how much came from the employee and how much from AI. As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to.
That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. Quite the opposite, in fact: 94% of the managers polled said they were excited to improve work using AI, and many are confident they know where to use it to get the most value. Michal Miller Levi, head of market research and customer insights at Monday.com, compared the enthusiasm to the early days of the internet in the 2000s, saying people see a similar kind of “magic” to AI.
But the problem, she told TechCrunch, is simply that AI is developing faster than companies can adapt. “AI works very well for [managers] individually, but they also have a different role as managers. They need to drive the organization as well … Their struggle is [due to] the fact that AI is just moving faster than the organizational processes,” Levi said.
Managers are also reconsidering how they judge their teams: 78% of respondents said they have changed how they evaluate employees after adopting AI, placing greater weight on how well staff can create prompts, decide which tasks to delegate to AI, and experiment with new ways of working.
But how fairly can employees be judged when managers can’t easily tell how much of their work was produced by AI? And what if the managers themselves are increasingly relying on AI to make those judgments? The survey found that 46% of managers use AI to help inform their decisions, and 39% of leaders are using AI to draft performance reviews.
That practice runs the risk of introducing even more bias than usual into the review process, given that LLMs are, at their core, prediction machines and tend to repeat human patterns found in their training data. Research from the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research earlier this year
found that
“in the absence of clear objective standards and when individuals are rated independently,” LLMs tend to rate performance similarly to humans. And a
research paper
in early 2025 found that AI models can be biased against black male candidates, and “demonstrate significant biases, varying in terms of the directions and magnitudes across different social groups.”
When I asked Levi whether using AI to weigh in on people’s performance could introduce outside bias into the process, she said companies have yet to work out how to handle such issues.
AI is also changing what a manager’s day looks like. Someone has to decide which tasks to hand over to AI agents, check what they produce, and step in when something goes wrong. The report suggests that this supervision could amount to a new layer of “invisible labor.”
The software itself is becoming harder to manage. Fifty-seven percent of managers say their organizations now have more tools in circulation than before, and about 51% said their tools had grown more interdependent and clustered since adopting AI. Only 29% described their AI infrastructure as fully optimized and centralized.
Levi said businesses had expected AI to help shrink their software stacks. Instead, they’re dealing with more apps, integrations, and shadow AI usage as employees adopt tools outside their companies’ approved systems.
“Managers completed 2025 with the feeling that they will consolidate tools, actually, that they’ll reduce the number of software. But what happened is that the number of tools that they’re using increased,” Levi said. “More than 50% are saying that they’re using more tools now than they did last year, and it’s not stopping.”
This need for control seems to be growing urgent as companies deploy AI agents that can act on their own. The survey found that 58% of managers expect to oversee more AI agents than human employees within the next year, and 46% worry about losing control over those agents’ actions.
There’s also quite a bit of fear over being held responsible for decisions made by AI (35% of respondents said so), as LLMs are still largely unpredictable. “They don’t want their agents to be fully autonomous,” Levi said, explaining that managers want people to be involved and consulted by AI when it comes to crucial tasks and decisions.
At heart, the report’s findings show that AI adoption is increasingly becoming as much a governance problem as it is an opportunity to raise productivity. Without proper processes and infrastructure to deal with it, managers seem to be scrambling to keep things chugging.

, the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.
“The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant,” Meta says in the press release. Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, added during an earnings call that the new class of shares will “expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI.”
Meta has poured
billions of dollars into the AI race
as it builds (
and promotes
) sprawling data centers,
poaches top talent
from other companies like OpenAI, and builds AI models capable of rivaling those from other tech giants. The company expects capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from the previous $130 billion and $145 billion estimate.

Meta says it would’ve made over $22 billion if it didn’t have to pay a child safety settlement
It’s been a busy past few weeks for Meta,
which launched its AI agent, Muse
, in September. Like other AI agents, Muse can do things like clean out your email inbox, book restaurant reservations, and plan trips. The Muse app shot to the top of app stores shortly after its rollout, and
hit 10 million downloads
in the US this week. Meta also rolled out its
Muse Wonder model this week
.
Muse’s launch hasn’t come without some snags. Amid
concerns about user privacy
, a tech YouTuber
reported that the agent
gave out his address to a stranger on Facebook Marketplace. The company has also
had to pause Muse’s conversation-sharing feature
after researchers discovered chats publicly available on the web.

Anthropic just announced an AI agent competitor to Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots: Claude Duet. The new agent, designed for professionals and small business owners, is launching as a “research preview,”
according to Anthropic
, and it’s available as a standalone app on iOS and Android and through Claude on the web.
The AI agent is built around Claude Opus 5.5. Here’s Anthropic’s description of what it can do:
Each morning, it sends you a short brief on the most important items across your connected apps. Throughout the day, it keeps tabs on those apps and messages you only when something needs your attention. You can also hand it tasks of all shapes—from simple administrative tasks of scheduling meetings to more complex ones, such as building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps.
Claude Duet pulls in memory, skills, and connected apps from Claude, and it has a virtual machine with a browser that it can use for completing work. Before any big step, like sending a payment or deleting something, Claude Duet messages you for approval. Given that Duet may be taking action on sensitive information, it has a new “new dedicated classifier and safety system prompt” that are “designed to reject requests to share the strictest tier of information,” such as credit card numbers.
Anthropic says Claude Duet is currently an “early version” and that it “still might misread a thread or miscalibrate what’s urgent.” It’s also not “as strong” at personal errands like booking tickets.
If you want to try Claude Duet, you can
get on the waitlist
, though you’ll need to be a Pro or Max subscriber in the US to use it.
